title: Saving a different Part Status asks to confirm first
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Create an active part, part A, for this test.
  • Start on the Inventory page, on the Active tab, with part A's part number typed in the Search box.
custom_steps:
1. Click the part A row.
  2. Click Inactive under Part Status.
  3. Click Save.
  4. Click Cancel in the confirmation.
  5. Click Cancel.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Edit Inventory Part opens with a green "Active" pill.

Step 2:

  • Inactive is picked, and nothing is applied yet: the pill still reads a green "Active".

Step 3:

  • Before anything changes, a confirmation titled "Deactivate part?" opens over the part window.
  • It is the app's standard confirmation: a title with a close X at its right, message lines, a "Note (Optional)" field, Cancel and a red Deactivate button, and there is no word to type to confirm.

Step 4:

  • The confirmation closes.

Step 5:

  • The window closes and part A is still on the Active tab.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Parts Lifecycle Update", Confluence 829227015, version 35 (edited 27 Oct 2026 by Chris Ward), read 28 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-10647, story SV-10823 (Story 10, Confirming and Recording a Status Change), story SV-10826 (Story 13, The Part Dialog)

  • S10-R1: “A status change is confirmed before it is applied, from either entry point: the bulk bar (Stories 2 and 3), or Save in the part dialog after the user picks a different Part Status (S13-R21).”
  • S10-R2: “The confirmation is the application's standard confirmation dialog. There is no confirmation word to type.”
  • S13-R21: “Picking a different status changes nothing until Save. When Save is pressed with a different status picked, the confirmation of Story 10 opens first.”
  • Key Decisions: “Every confirmation is the application's standard dialog. A title with the close X, a message, an optional note, Cancel and a confirm button. There is no confirmation word to type.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
